runtimes.finding: DEPENDENCY_OVER_INSTALL_CONFIRMED. The Dockerfile pulls rapidsai/base:26.08-cuda12-py3.13-amd64 -- the full prebuilt RAPIDS suite -- but the service's own code only ever imports cudf and cugraph (both lazily, inside function bodies) plus fastapi/pydantic/pyarrow for the HTTP boundary. This is the exact 'installed a whole framework for one primitive' pattern DEPENDENCY-CAPABILITY-GUARD-01 exists to prevent. NVIDIA's own RAPIDS docs recommend a custom image with only the needed libraries for exactly this reason (smaller image, narrower attack/maintenance surface). Not fixed in this pass -- flagged as a real, verified finding for a future minimal-rebuild task, not silently left unrecorded.

tile.programming.gpu (cuTile).gate: ACE-RADIX-01 full PASS on a CUDA 13.2+ host (this dev host's CUDA 13.0 toolkit ships only a compiler-intrinsic stub, per root CLAUDE.md's ACE-RADIX-01 result: cuTile went stable on Ampere at CUDA 13.2, not 13.0)
tile.programming.gpu (cuTile).note: CUDA 13.3 (toolkit/runtime release) is NOT cuTile (Python DSL for the tile programming model) is NOT Tensor Cores (hardware units, 3rd-gen on this RTX 3060 Ti / Ampere sm_86). SIMT is the existing execution model cuGraph/cuDF/CuPy kernels already use; tile programming coexists with it per-kernel, it does not replace it. Do not install cuTile toolchain (cuda-tile, TileIR/compiler components) until a benchmark gate explicitly proves a graph or projection kernel needs it -- Jaccard/BFS/connected-components/irregular graph traversal are not Tensor-Core-shaped workloads and do not motivate this.
